turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’m having significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing. I also have a cough that produces colored or more abundant sputum than usual, and a sore throat. My symptoms are more prominent at night. I have COPD and I smoke cigarettes. I also have some sensitive burning pain (intensity 2/10) in my right side of the chest/upper chest and my left breast and posterior chest wall, plus pain in the pharynx.
Have you had a fever or chills, and if so, what has been the highest temperature?
Is the chest pain worse when you take a deep breath or cough?
Has this shortness of breath and cough gotten significantly worse compared to your usual COPD baseline, or is this a completely new type of breathing difficulty?
Have you noticed your sputum has changed color to yellow
Do you need to prop yourself up with pillows to breathe comfortably when lying down, or do the breathing difficulties wake you up suddenly at night?
I don’t know. My symptoms are more prominent at night, but I don’t know if I wake up suddenly or need to prop myself up with pillows.
Have you noticed any blood in your sputum, or have you felt confused or unusually sleepy during the day?
Can you speak in full sentences without stopping to catch your breath, or do you find yourself unable to complete sentences due to the breathing difficulty?
Have you been around anyone with a cold or respiratory infection recently, or did these symptoms start after what seemed like a common cold?
